import seaborn as sns

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
file_path = 'data/dogs_zurich.csv'
dogs_df = pd.read_csv(file_path)

# Prepare data for visualization
breed_counts = dogs_df['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().head(10)
district_counts = dogs_df['KreisLang'].value_counts().head(10)

# Set up the matplotlib figure
fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(10, 12))

# Plot 1: Top 10 Dog Breeds
sns.barplot(x=breed_counts.values, y=breed_counts.index, ax=ax[0], palette='viridis')
ax[0].set_title('Top 10 Dog Breeds in Zurich')
ax[0].set_xlabel('Number of Dogs')
ax[0].set_ylabel('Breed')

# Plot 2: Top 10 Districts with Most Dogs
sns.barplot(x=district_counts.values, y=district_counts.index, ax=ax[1], palette='magma')
ax[1].set_title('Top 10 Districts with Most Dogs in Zurich')
ax[1].set_xlabel('Number of Dogs')
ax[1].set_ylabel('District')

# Adjust the layout
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
